xs-options(1) ​

Option reference

Every option, with stable links, what it implies, and what a remote helper must support.

SOURCE ​

Captured from xs version 0.1.0 protocol version 4 git 1fff2a09ae2c. Every option xs --help lists is below, with a stable link: options.html#delete for a long option, options.html#z for its short form. Open Details for what each one implies, which remote-helper features it needs, and where it is explained.

Original help ↓   /   Manpage ↓   /   Option data (JSON) ↓

0 of 0 options

OPTIONS (SAME MEANING AS RSYNC) ​

OptionDescription
-v, --verboseincrease verbosity
Details

Repeat for more detail: -vv adds the limiting-stage estimate (reading, network or writing) to progress and to the final summary.

See Progress & output › File Output And Logs

-q, --quietsuppress non-error messages
Details

Suppresses progress, file lines and the dry-run plan. Errors and the end-of-run error summary still print.

See Progress & output › Output Streams

-c, --checksumskip based on checksum, not mod-time & size
Details

Both sides hash candidate files; progress shows verifying N checks. A content difference with matching size and time is reported as c in the change code.

See Itemize & out-format › Changes · Progress & output › Phases

-a, --archivearchive mode; equals -rlptgoD
Details

Does not imply -H, -A, -X, -U, -N, -E or --fileflags. With --files-from, -a does not enable recursion; add -r.

Implies -r -l -p -t -g -o -D

See Metadata & filesystems › Archive Mode

-r, --recursiverecurse into directories
Details

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

-d, --dirstransfer directories without recursing
Details

Copies named directories without their contents. Implied by --files-from.

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

-R, --relative
helper feature
preserve source path components and implied directories
Details

A /./ component cuts off the prefix: xs -aR /data/./project/file dest/ creates dest/project/file. Implied directories get their source attributes. --no-implied-dirs still delegates to rsync.

Remote helpers must support PF_RELATIVE. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Transfers & paths › Relative Paths And Selection

--files-from=FILE
helper feature
select source names from FILE ("-" reads stdin)
Details

Names are relative to the single source directory. - reads stdin, :FILE reads the list on the remote machine of the transfer. Leading slashes refer to the source root and .. cannot escape it. Use -0 for NUL-delimited lists.

Implies -R -d

Remote helpers must support PF_FILES_FROM. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Transfers & paths › Relative Paths And Selection · Filters & mirroring › File Lists

--list-only
helper feature
list source entries; do not transfer or change DEST
Details

Lists sources and leaves DEST untouched. A single source argument with no DEST lists it too.

Remote helpers must support PF_LIST. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Transfers & paths › Listing

-X, --xattrs
helper feature
preserve extended attributes (twice includes rsync internals)
Details

-XX also copies rsync-internal attributes. Whole-directory clones are disabled so each entry is handled individually. Large values spill to a temporary file beyond an 8 MiB in-memory budget.

Remote helpers must support PF_XATTRS, PF_XATTR_STREAM. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Hard Links, Acls, And Xattrs

-H, --hard-links
helper feature
preserve hard links within the transferred tree
Details

Preserves link groups among selected files, including across directories. Links to files outside the selection are not recreated.

Remote helpers must support PF_HLINK. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Itemize & out-format › Hard Links

-S, --sparse
helper feature
create holes for zero-filled file regions
Details

Disables cloning. Works with delta, resumed and in-place writes.

Remote helpers must support PF_SPARSE. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Sparse And Special Files

--link-dest=DIR
helper feature
reuse unchanged files from a previous snapshot
Details

Up to 20 directories. Relative paths start at the destination directory. Unchanged files with matching requested metadata become hard links; others are copied, and a snapshot can still serve as their delta basis.

Remote helpers must support PF_LINK_DEST. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Resume & snapshots › Snapshot Reuse

-l, --linkscopy symlinks as symlinks
Details

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

--safe-links
helper feature
skip symlinks that point outside the transfer tree
Details

Skips links that point outside the transfer tree and protects their existing destination entries from deletion.

Remote helpers must support PF_SAFE_LINKS. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Compatibility › Behavioral Differences

-L, --copy-linkstransform symlink into referent file/dir
Details

Overrides -l. Metadata options such as -A and --fileflags then apply to the referent.

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

-p, --permspreserve permissions
Details

See Metadata & filesystems › Archive Mode

--chmod=CHMODchange incoming file/directory permissions
Details

Numeric modes or comma-separated symbolic rules; D/F restrict a rule to directories or files, and repeated options append rules. Disables whole-directory clones. Works with protocol-3 helpers, because it changes existing mode fields.

See Metadata & filesystems › Permission And Owner Overrides

-E, --executability
helper feature
preserve executability of regular files
Details

Only matters when --perms is off. Apple’s system rsync uses -E for extended attributes; use the long name when fallback must be unambiguous.

Remote helpers must support PF_EXECUTABILITY. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Permission And Owner Overrides

--fileflags
macOS onlyhelper feature
preserve BSD file flags (macOS)
Details

Adds a twelfth change-code character. On Linux the option is refused natively; fallback then needs an rsync built with --fileflags, which standard upstream builds are not.

Remote helpers must support PF_FILEFLAGS. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags · Itemize & out-format › The Change Code

-o, --owner
helper feature
preserve owner (super-user only)
Details

Names map between hosts unless --numeric-ids is set; the name mapping needs the helper feature.

Remote helpers must support PF_IDMAP. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Archive Mode

-g, --group
helper feature
preserve group
Details

Remote helpers must support PF_IDMAP. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Archive Mode

--chown=USER:GROUP
helper feature
change destination owner/group (names or IDs)
Details

Names resolve on the destination host. Either field may be omitted. On a push, overrides still apply after a later --no-owner/--no-group.

Implies -o -g

Remote helpers must support PF_CHOWN. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Permission And Owner Overrides

-Dsame as --devices --specials
Details

Device nodes need privilege on the receiver. --no-D turns both off.

Implies --devices --specials

See Itemize & out-format › Changes

-A, --acls
helper feature
preserve ACLs (implies --perms)
Details

Remote ACLs need matching styles: macOS to macOS, or Linux to Linux. A macOS ↔ Linux request delegates before any write, and rsync itself rejects the tested cross-platform ACLs. Principals map by name unless --numeric-ids.

Implies -p

Remote helpers must support PF_ACL_POSIX, PF_ACL_DARWIN, PF_ACL_UUID. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Hard Links, Acls, And Xattrs

-t, --timespreserve modification times
Details

See Itemize & out-format › The Change Code

-U, --atimes
helper feature
preserve file access times (twice enables --open-noatime)
Details

Files and special inodes only; directories and symlinks keep rsync’s omission. -UU also requests O_NOATIME reads.

Remote helpers must support PF_ATIMES. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags

-N, --crtimes
macOS onlyhelper feature
preserve creation times (macOS)
Details

Including directories and symlinks. On Linux the option is refused and handed to rsync.

Remote helpers must support PF_CRTIMES. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags

--open-noatime
helper feature
avoid read access-time updates where supported
Details

May need file ownership or privilege. macOS ignores the flag.

Remote helpers must support PF_OPEN_NOATIME. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags

-O, --omit-dir-timesomit directory modification/access/creation times
Details

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags

-J, --omit-link-timesomit symlink modification/access/creation times
Details

See Metadata & filesystems › Times And File Flags

-n, --dry-runperform a trial run with no changes made
Details

Always ends with would transfer N files (X), delete M on stdout, even without -v.

See Filters & mirroring › Preview A Mirror

-W, --whole-filesend the whole file; disable resume and block matching
Details

Disables both verified-prefix resume and block matching, locally and remotely.

See Resume & snapshots › Delta And Whole-File Transfers

--no-whole-fileenable verified-prefix resume again
Details

See Resume & snapshots › Partial Transfers

-x, --one-file-systemdon't cross filesystem boundaries
Details

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

-e, --rsh=COMMANDspecify the remote shell to use
Details

Precedence: -e, then XSYNC_RSH, then RSYNC_RSH, then a shell in XSYNC_OPTS, then config, then ssh.

See SSH & remote helpers › Examples · Environment & defaults › Remote Shell Precedence

--rsync-path=PROGRAMspecify the xs to run on the remote machine
Details

Bypasses the automatic helper lookup. The same command is kept if the transfer falls back, so it must then accept rsync’s server arguments too.

See SSH & remote helpers › Helper Lookup

--no-fallbackfail instead of re-executing rsync for missing support
Details

An option xs does not implement then exits 1; a helper missing a needed feature exits 4; a missing helper exits 127.

See Compatibility › Fallback · Troubleshooting › Fallback Notices

--fallbackenable fallback (overrides XSYNC_FALLBACK=0)
Details

See Compatibility › Fallback

--existingskip creating new files on receiver
Details

See Transfers & paths › Existing Files

--ignore-existingskip updating files that exist on receiver
Details

See Transfers & paths › Existing Files

--deletedelete extraneous files from dest dirs
Details

Also accepted: --del/--delete-during, --delete-before, --delete-delay and --delete-after. Source I/O errors suppress deletion unless --ignore-errors.

See Filters & mirroring › Preview A Mirror

--delete-after
helper feature
scan deletions and merge files after transfer
Details

Scans the destination after transfers finish and reloads receiver merge files from the updated tree.

Remote helpers must support PF_DELETE_AFTER. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Filters & mirroring › Merge Files

-m, --prune-empty-dirs
helper feature
omit empty directory chains from the file list
Details

Protected empty directories and their ancestors are kept.

Remote helpers must support PF_PRUNE_EMPTY. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Filters & mirroring › Exclude And Include

--delete-excludedalso delete excluded files from dest dirs
Details

Makes unqualified include/exclude rules sender-only. Explicit receiver rules still protect entries.

See Filters & mirroring › Source And Receiver Rules

--ignore-errorsdelete even when the sender encountered I/O errors
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Preview A Mirror

--max-delete=NUMdelete at most NUM entries (exit 25 if exceeded)
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Preview A Mirror · Exit status & errors › Exit Status

--forceforce deletion of dirs even if not empty
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Preview A Mirror

--max-size=SIZEdon't transfer any file larger than SIZE
Details

Sizes accept K/M/G/T (binary) and KB/MB/GB/TB (decimal) suffixes.

--min-size=SIZEdon't transfer any file smaller than SIZE
Details

Same size syntax as --max-size.

--bwlimit=RATE
helper feature
limit bytes sent/copied per second (bare RATE: KiB/s)
Details

Bare numbers are KiB/s; suffixes K–P, KiB/MiB or decimal KB/MB are accepted and rounded to the nearest KiB/s. Zero disables the limit; nonzero rates below 512 bytes/s are rejected. Remote writers limit bytes after compression; local workers share one limit on bytes written, which disables APFS cloning.

Remote helpers must support PF_IO_CONTROL. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See SSH & remote helpers › Bandwidth And Timeouts

--timeout=SECONDS
helper feature
remote idle I/O timeout (0 disables; exits with code 30)
Details

Integer seconds. Covers shell and handshake waits, partial frames, blocked writes and a helper that stays alive after the protocol ends. Keep-alives are sent at most every 10 seconds, or a third of the timeout.

Remote helpers must support PF_IO_CONTROL. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See SSH & remote helpers › Bandwidth And Timeouts

--partialkeep partially transferred files
Details

Current helpers verify an existing destination prefix with XXH3-128 on both sides and send only the rest. Files up to 512 KiB use the whole-file path.

See Resume & snapshots › Partial Transfers

--inplaceupdate destination files in-place
Details

Writes destination files directly. A delta basis is snapshotted so moved blocks are preserved while the original inode is updated.

See Resume & snapshots › Atomic And In-Place Output

--mkpathcreate the destination's path component
Details

See Transfers & paths › Local Copy

--numeric-idsdon't map uid/gid values by user/group name
Details

See Metadata & filesystems › Hard Links, Acls, And Xattrs

-u, --updateskip files that are newer on the receiver
Details

See Transfers & paths › Existing Files

-I, --ignore-timesdon't skip files that match size and time
--size-onlyskip files that match in size
-@, --modify-window=NUMset the accuracy for mod-time comparisons
-z, --compresscompress file data during the transfer (zstd)
Details

zstd, decompressed on several threads. Has no effect on local copies. A helper without compression support silently gets plain data. --compress-choice accepts only zstd or none.

See Transfers & paths › Ssh Push And Pull

--compress-level=NUMexplicitly set compression level
Details

See Transfers & paths › Ssh Push And Pull

-f, --filter=RULE
helper feature
add a file-filtering RULE
Details

Supports +/-, H/S, P/R, !, merge rules, and the modifiers ! / s r p x. Plain include/exclude rules work with any helper; side, merge and CVS rules need the corresponding features.

Remote helpers must support PF_FILTERS, PF_MERGE_FILTERS, PF_CVS_FILTERS. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Filters & mirroring › Source And Receiver Rules · Filters & mirroring › Merge Files

-F
helper feature
merge .rsync-filter files (twice also excludes them)
Details

Same as --filter=': /.rsync-filter', including ancestor files. -FF also excludes the filter files.

Remote helpers must support PF_MERGE_FILTERS. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Filters & mirroring › Merge Files

-C, --cvs-exclude
helper feature
exclude CVS defaults and .cvsignore patterns
Details

Adds per-directory .cvsignore files, built-in CVS exclusions, $HOME/.cvsignore and CVSIGNORE after explicit rules.

Remote helpers must support PF_CVS_FILTERS. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Filters & mirroring › Merge Files

--exclude=PATTERNexclude files matching PATTERN
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Exclude And Include

--exclude-from=FILEread exclude patterns from FILE
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Exclude And Include

--include=PATTERNdon't exclude files matching PATTERN
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Exclude And Include

--include-from=FILEread include patterns from FILE
Details

See Filters & mirroring › Exclude And Include

-0, --from0use NUL delimiters in list and filter merge files
Details

Applies to file lists, include/exclude files and merge files opened after the option. --no-from0 restores line mode.

See Filters & mirroring › File Lists

--statsgive some file-transfer stats
Details

See Progress & output › Units And Pipes

-h, --human-readableuse 1000-based units (-hh uses 1024)
Details

One rule everywhere: decimal units by default and with -h, binary with -hh. --no-h removes digit separators. JSON counters are never scaled.

See Progress & output › Units And Pipes

--progress[=json]show progress (default on terminals), or JSON events
Details

On by default when stderr is a terminal. On a pipe, plain --progress prints one line per second; --info=progress2 prints rsync’s line shape; --progress=json prints events.

See Progress & output › Terminal Progress · JSON progress events › Synopsis

--no-progresssuppress progress; XSYNC_PROGRESS=0 also disables it
Details

See Environment & defaults › Environment

-Psame as --partial --progress
Details

Implies --partial --progress

See Resume & snapshots › Partial Transfers

-i, --itemize-changesoutput a change-summary for all updates
Details

See Itemize & out-format › The Change Code

-8, --8-bit-outputretain high bytes in names; escape unsafe control bytes
Details

See Itemize & out-format › Order, Logs And Escaping

--out-format=FORMAT
helper feature
file lines: %i %n %L %l %o %f %b %t %% (optional width)
Details

Remote helpers must support PF_OUTPUT, PF_DIR_OUTPUT. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Itemize & out-format › --Out-Format

--log-file=FILE
helper feature
append the same stdout stream to FILE
Details

Remote helpers must support PF_OUTPUT. A helper without it causes fallback, or exit 4 with --no-fallback.

See Itemize & out-format › Order, Logs And Escaping

--version, --helpprint the version, or this help, and exit

XS EXTENSIONS ​

OptionDescription
--install=HOST
xs only
explicitly install the matching release at ~/.local/bin refuses newer versions unless --force is supplied
Details

Never part of a transfer. Release files are found beside the executable, in a sibling dist/, in ../share/xs/releases/, or in XSYNC_RELEASE_DIR. An interrupted upload leaves the previous executable in place.

See SSH & remote helpers › Explicit Remote Install · Install & releases › Remote Install

-j, --jobs=N
xs only
number of worker threads (default: performance cores)
Details

See How it works › Local Engine

--no-clone
xs only
always copy file data, even where a copy-on-write clone (APFS, same volume, with -pt) would be possible
Details

Clones only happen on the same APFS volume with at least -pt. They can carry xattrs, ACLs and access/creation times that -a alone would not copy.

See Metadata & filesystems › Apfs Clones

--atomic
xs only
create new files via temp file + rename (default)
Details

See Resume & snapshots › Atomic And In-Place Output

--no-atomic
xs only
create new byte-copied files directly (fewer renames; a crash can leave truncated files under final names)
Details

See Resume & snapshots › Atomic And In-Place Output

ALSO ACCEPTED ​

These rsync spellings work natively but are not listed in --help.

OptionMeaning
--delsame as --delete-during
--delete-beforedelete extraneous entries before transferring
--delete-duringdelete extraneous entries while transferring
--delete-delayfind deletions during the transfer, delete afterwards
--devicespreserve device files (part of -D)
--specialspreserve special files (part of -D)
--ignore-non-existingsame as --existing
--infoprogress2, progress0, stats2 or stats0, comma separated
--compress-choicezstd or none (alias --zc)
--cloneallow copy-on-write clones again after --no-clone
--no-OPTIONturn off a flag, for example --no-perms, --no-times, --no-D

DELEGATED TO RSYNC ​

xs does not implement these rsync options. A command that uses one runs a real rsync from PATH instead, with a one-line notice on stderr. With --no-fallback it exits 1. The list is read from the option parser in src/main.cpp.

--address --append --append-verify -b, --backup --backup-dir -B, --block-size --cc --checksum-choice --checksum-seed --compare-dest --contimeout --copy-as --copy-dest --copy-devices --copy-dirlinks --copy-unsafe-links --daemon --debug --delay-updates --delete-missing-args --early-input --fake-super --fsync -y, --fuzzy --groupmap --i-r --iconv --ignore-missing-args --implied-dirs --inc-recursive -4, --ipv4 -6, --ipv6 --keep-dirlinks --log-file-format --max-alloc --msgs2stderr --munge-links --new-compress --no-i-r --no-implied-dirs --no-inc-recursive --no-msgs2stderr --no-protect-args --old-args --old-compress --only-write-batch --outbuf --partial-dir --password-file --port --preallocate --read-batch -M, --remote-option --remove-source-files --skip-compress --sockopts --stop-after --stop-at --suffix --super -T, --temp-dir --trust-sender --usermap --write-batch --write-devices

See compatibility and troubleshooting.
